newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Dozens of corpses washed up on Burundi lake.
newsitem.headline: Dozens of corpses washed up on Burundi lake.

text.p: Dozens of bloated corpses, some with bound hands, are floating down the Rusizi river bordering on Zaire and Burundi into Lake Tanganyika, fishermen said on Thursday.
At least 13 corpses, including the body of a young child, were strewn along a one kilometre (half-mile) stretch of beach on the shore close to the mouth of the Rusizi at the northern end of the lake.
Fishermen said they had buried 50 and there were many more.
They did not know if the bodies were those of Rwandans, Burundians, or Zaireans, or who had killed them.
"There are lots and lots of corpses that have come down here. Most of them we just buried because they smelled so bad, perhaps 50 in all," one fisherman told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
"But there are lots more that just carried on out into the lake," the fisherman said.
They added there were also dozens more fresh corpses close to a Burundian military post on the shore of the blue lake.

It was unclear who was responsible for the bodies floating into the lake, reminiscent of the sight of thousands of corpses -- some with bound hands -- which floated into Lake Victoria during the 1994 genocide of up to one million people in Rwanda.

Some of the bodies had decomposed beyond recognition while others, pulled out onto the beach, appeared to have spent little time in water. Some had their hands tied behind their backs with wire, suggesting death by execution, while others were headless.
One skull, stripped clean, lay near the corpse of a man.

It was also unclear if the dead were Zaireans or Burundians, Hutus or Tutsis but they have been floating into the lake since Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops began fighting over the eastern Zairean town of Uvira facing Burundi nearly two weeks ago.
Burundian authorities said they were unaware of the existence of the corpses and said they could have been killed by the Zairean army but were not the victims of the Burundi military.

"It is completely false that there are bodies in the water and they were killed by the army. If there are bodies it is not because of us. Perhaps the Zairean military is still killing people," Gatumba zone chief Marie-Therese Ngurunziza said.

Ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels took control of the eastern Zairean town of Uvira last week and tens of thousands of Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fled camps north of Uvira because of the fighting.
Mortar fire from the direction of Uvira could clearly be heard at Gatumba from across Lake Taganyika on Thursday.
The Rusizi river borders on Burundi's northwest Cibitoke province and has been a crossing point for Hutu rebels infiltrating Burundi from camps in Zaire to fight Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army.
A total of 3,440 Burundian Hutu refugees returning home after fleeing Burundi's civil war have been registered at Gatumba, the United Nations High Commission for Refugees said.
